clue.text: Dandy feather in a Yankee's cap

definitions.meaning: an eighteenth-century fop who affected Continental fashions was called this
in the song Yankee Doodle, the hero stuck a feather in his cap and called it by this name

explanation.definitionFit: The word named the foppish young men of Georgian London, which is why the song mocks a bumpkin's feather with it.

clue.text: Cheeky tramp fuddled with ale

indicators.note: fuddled means muddled by drink, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunken vagrant gets lippy after too much beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuddled' rearranges TRAMP and ALE together.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adjective for impudent or saucy, from Old French for ill-spoken.

clue.text: Diminutive seer witnessed his demise

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme the fly says it saw the bird die 'with my little eye', so a small eye was the witness

explanation.walkthrough: 'Seer' looks like a prophet but is simply one who sees: the fly with its little eye in the nursery rhyme about the bird's death.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme asks who killed the bird and who saw him die; the fly answers with its little eye.

clue.text: Grip this murderer's son's companion

parts.note: Grip is the talking raven of a simple-minded Dickens hero whose father was a murderer; the answer is that family's surname

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grip' looks like a verb but is the name of the raven in the Dickens novel Barnaby Rudge, companion to Barnaby, whose father committed murder.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of Barnaby, the Dickens title character, whose father was the murderer and whose pet raven was called Grip.

clue.text: Selfless, bliss, small advantage in rain storm

indicators.note: the short word for advantage sits inside the rearranged rain
a storm whips things about, so the letters of rain are thrown into a new order

parts.note: van is the shortened tennis term for advantage

explanation.surface: Some calm inner happiness, plus a slight edge, amid a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' turns RAIN into NIRA, and 'in' puts VAN inside it, after NIR. VAN is tennis shorthand for advantage, the point after deuce.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buddhist goal is a blissful state in which the self is extinguished.

clue.text: Love's a goddess? A god

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O, and the 's adds S
Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow

explanation.surface: A query whether the beloved is divine, answered by naming a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is nil in tennis scoring, written as O; the apostrophe-s supplies S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian deity of the underworld and rebirth, husband of Isis.

clue.text: Dubious old citizen turns up in various places

indicators.note: the reversed citizen word sits within the rearranged places
various suggests the letters of places taking differing positions
in a down clue, turns up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: cit is an old, disparaging short form for a townsman or citizen

explanation.surface: A doubting veteran townsman keeps appearing all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges PLACES as SCEPAL and 'turns up' reverses CIT; 'in' places the result between SCEP and AL. CIT was a dated sneer for a town tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtful or disbelieving, an exact synonym in the sense of not being convinced.

clue.text: Smiling in the Austrian Tyrol

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone beaming happily in the Alpine region of Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the end of 'Austrian' and the first letter of 'Tyrol'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare adjective from French meaning cheerful or laughing.

clue.text: Just the ticket for a bachelor

definitions.meaning: a one-way rail ticket is called this in Britain
an unmarried man is described this way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the ticket' sounds like 'exactly right', but here it names the British one-way fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way fare in Britain and an unmarried person share the word, as a noun for the fare and an adjective for marital status.

clue.text: Jael hit the nail on the head-did him no good

definitions.text: Jael hit the nail on the head-did him no good

parts.words: Jael hit the nail on the head-did him no good
parts.note: in the Book of Judges Jael drives a tent peg through the temple of a sleeping Canaanite general, so hitting the nail on the head was literal

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for being exactly right is taken literally: Jael hammered a tent peg into the Canaanite commander's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canaanite general in Judges 4 killed by Jael with a tent peg while he slept.

clue.text: With a bit of luck the champion gets clear

indicators.note: a bit of means only a small part of the word luck is taken, its opening

parts.note: El Cid, the Castilian hero, was called the Campeador, the champion

explanation.surface: A fortunate winner emerges with a clear lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' takes LU from 'luck'. CID is the Spanish hero El Cid, whose title Campeador means champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily understood or transparent, as lucid prose is plain.

clue.text: How Adam and Eve create a disturbance

definitions.meaning: the first parents brought up their elder son, so they literally reared him
an idiom for making trouble or an uproar

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase says the first couple brought up their son; as an idiom it means kicking up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for making an uproar, taken literally, describes Genesis parents rearing their firstborn.

clue.text: Payable to bearer in drink a long time after

indicators.note: after places the long-time word behind the drink

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A cheque to whoever holds it, cashed in a pub long afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Payable to bearer' sounds like cheque language, but a bearer here is a carrier of luggage, and the answer is the fee paid to one.
explanation.definitionFit: The charge made by a carrier for hauling goods or luggage is due to that carrier.

clue.text: Some say the lot

definitions.meaning: some said aloud is sum, and a sum is an amount added up
the whole amount, everything

explanation.walkthrough: 'Some say' is a sound-alike for 'sum', which means an amount added up.
explanation.definitionFit: An added-up sum and the whole of something are both meanings of the word, as noun and adjective.

clue.text: Complaint Fritz spotted ?

parts.note: Fritz is old slang for a German, and spotted describes the rash, so the illness is a German one with spots

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fritz' is dated British slang for a German; 'spotted' looks like 'noticed' but describes a rash. The illness is commonly called German measles.
explanation.definitionFit: The viral infection with a red rash is popularly known as German measles.

clue.text: At home in Oxford a hopeless undertaking

definitions.meaning: Matthew Arnold called Oxford the home of these, and the university city is still teased with the phrase
an effort certain to fail

explanation.walkthrough: Matthew Arnold described Oxford as the 'home of lost causes', so the phrase belongs there.
explanation.definitionFit: A doomed effort is the idiom's meaning, and Arnold's famous description of the English university city uses it.

clue.text: Somewhat curvaceous lady left out of rustic paradise

parts.note: an arc is a gentle curve, a somewhat curving line

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is removed from lady

explanation.surface: A slightly curvy woman is excluded from an idyllic countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes L from LADY, leaving ADY.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic form of Arcadia, the idealised pastoral land of Greek legend.

clue.text: Lion-tamer dared, it is said, to be too smart

indicators.note: it is said tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the biblical Daniel, Dan for short, survived the lions' den and defied the king, so Dan defied

explanation.surface: A bold animal trainer is apparently overdressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Daniel, shortened to Dan, tamed the lions in the den; 'dared' gives defied. 'Dan defied' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed up like a fop, overly stylish.

clue.text: Increase-egg supplier includes following number

indicators.note: includes puts the number within the bird

parts.note: a hen lays eggs
eight is a number

explanation.surface: A rise in production as a poultry farmer adds the next number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' is only a link here, and 'egg supplier' sounds like a shop but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise or intensify something, a verb meaning to make greater.

clue.text: Strange noises affecting Cyprus and Greece

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of noises are set out oddly

explanation.surface: Odd sounds in the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges NOISES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek Cypriot movement for political union of the island with the Greek mainland.

clue.text: Do we put our shirts on those who run thus ?

definitions.text: Do we put our shirts on those who run thus ?

parts.words: Do we put our shirts on those who run thus
parts.note: to put one's shirt on a runner is to bet heavily, but these runners wear no shirts at all

explanation.walkthrough: 'put our shirts on' is a betting idiom; read literally, it means clothing people who run naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Running naked through a public place, as at sports grounds.

clue.text: Sign for what's left

definitions.meaning: Libra, the scales, is a sign of the zodiac
the remainder, as in a bank account

explanation.walkthrough: Libra is represented by scales, so the zodiac sign is this; the remainder in an account is too.
explanation.definitionFit: The scales of Libra and the remaining sum in an account both carry the name.

clue.text: Gun emplacement has to be charged

definitions.meaning: a group of artillery pieces in position
an electrical cell that needs charging

explanation.walkthrough: In law the word also means an assault charge, a third sense lurking behind 'charged'.
explanation.definitionFit: An artillery unit and an electric cell are both named this; one is recharged.

clue.text: Building of service to a printers' association

definitions.meaning: a place of worship where services are held
a branch of a printers' trade union in a print shop is called this

explanation.walkthrough: A print-works union branch has traditionally been called by this church word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small place of Christian worship, and the traditional name for a printing-office trade union branch.

clue.text: Cry of Caesar's vengeful spirit

parts.note: in Julius Caesar, Antony foresees the ghost of Caesar ranging for revenge and shouting the order to slaughter

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Antony says Caesar's spirit will 'Cry Havoc! and let slip the dogs of war'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry was an old military order for pillage, used in Antony's speech in Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Goddess of the hearth used to light the fire

definitions.meaning: the Roman deity of home and hearth fire
a brand of short wax match was called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is an old brand of match.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity of the household fire lent her name to a kind of match.

clue.text: Sailor's without one on limitation of supplies

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the sailor surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a rating is a non-officer sailor in the Royal Navy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A seaman lacking one item while supplies are cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old sense of outside, so the sailor wraps the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Restricting how much of scarce goods each person may have.

clue.text: Old characters wild to start Hogmanay

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run riot into a new arrangement
to start takes only the opening stretch of the word Hogmanay

explanation.surface: Ancient letters go wild at the beginning of New Year's Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes HOGMA from the front of HOGMANAY, the Scottish New Year's Eve; 'wild' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Celtic alphabet of notched strokes, found on standing stones.

clue.text: Assume mail delayed about mid-January

indicators.note: about says the mail and delayed words go round the middle letter

parts.note: post is mail
late means delayed

indicators.note: mid takes the central letter of January

explanation.surface: Presume the post is held up around the middle of January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid' takes U, the middle letter of JANUARY; 'about' puts POSTLATE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward as true without proof, a verb meaning to take as given.

clue.text: Part, of flag, one shot to pieces

indicators.note: shot to pieces means broken up, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A flag partly destroyed by a single bullet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pieces' rearranges I and SHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a flag nearest the staff is a technical sense of the word, as is the vertical width.

clue.text: Liable to be fired, being drunk

definitions.meaning: a gun with ammunition in it is ready to shoot
slang for intoxicated

explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests losing a job, but it is a gun with a charge in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun with a round in it and an inebriated person share the slang adjective.

clue.text: Fielder, on my right, is a servant of the law '

indicators.note: on places the fielder after the my-right pieces

parts.note: mid-on is a cricket fielding position

explanation.surface: A cricketer standing to my right is a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: MID-ON is a cricket fielding position near the bowler on the leg side. The answer, from Achilles' followers, means an underling who obeys orders, here a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally Achilles' loyal soldiers, the word came to mean a hireling or minor officer of justice.
